ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$. Point P is a moving point on side $AC$, and line $PQ$ is drawn parallel to $AB$ intersecting $BC$ at point Q. Point D is the midpoint of segment $PQ$, and $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Given $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQC$ and $AB=13$, $BC=12$, find the length of $AP$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle C=90^\circ$ and $AB=13$, $BC=12$, it follows that $AC= \sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}} = \sqrt{13^{2}-12^{2}} =5$. Given that $PQ\parallel AB$, it implies that $\angle BAD=\angle ADP$. Furthermore, since $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, we have $\angle BAD=\angle PAD$, which leads to $\angle ADP=\angle PAD$, thus $PA=PD$. Given that $D$ is the midpoint of segment $PQ$, we have $PD= \frac{1}{2}PQ$, hence $QP=2PA. Since \triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQC$, it follows that $\frac{CP}{CA}=\frac{PQ}{AB}$, which means $\frac{5-AP}{5}=\frac{2AP}{13}$. Solving this gives $AP=\boxed{\frac{65}{23}}$.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 图像显示直角三角形ABC中，C为直角，AC水平、BC竖直，P在AC上，Q在BC上，PQ与AB平行，D是PQ的中点，AD从A连到D并平分角BAC。按坐标法求解：由AB=13、BC=12且∠C=90°，得AC=sqrt(13^2-12^2)=5。设C=(0,0)，A=(5,0)，B=(0,12)。令P=(p,0)，则AP=5-p。AB的斜率为(12-0)/(0-5)=-12/5。因为PQ∥AB，过P的直线斜率也是-12/5，其方程为y=-(12/5)(x-p)，与y轴BC交于Q=(0,12p/5)。D是PQ中点，所以D=(p/2,6p/5)。接着求A处内角平分线方向：从A指向C的单位向量是(-1,0)，从A指向B的单位向量是(-5/13,12/13)，两者相加方向为(-18/13,12/13)，等价于方向向量(-18,12)，斜率为12/(-18)=-2/3。因此AD方程为y=-(2/3)(x-5)。由于D在AD上，代入D=(p/2,6p/5)：6p/5=-(2/3)(p/2-5)=(10-p)/3。解得18p/5=10-p，即18p=50-5p，23p=50，所以p=50/23。于是AP=5-p=5-50/23=65/23。

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$. Point $P$ is a moving point on side $AC$, and line $PQ$ is drawn parallel to $AB$, intersecting $BC$ at point $Q$. Point $D$ is the midpoint of segment $PQ$, and $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Given $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQC$ and $AB=13$, $BC=12$, find the length of $AP$.
raw_record.answer: Since $\angle C=90^\circ$ and $AB=13$, $BC=12$, it follows that $AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BC^{2}}=\sqrt{13^{2}-12^{2}}=5$. Given that $PQ\parallel AB$, it implies that $\angle BAD=\angle ADP$. Furthermore, since $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, we have $\angle BAD=\angle PAD$, which leads to $\angle ADP=\angle PAD$, thus $PA=PD$. Given that $D$ is the midpoint of segment $PQ$, we have $PD=\frac{1}{2}PQ$, hence $QP=2PA$. Since $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQC$, it follows that $\frac{CP}{CA}=\frac{PQ}{AB}$, which means $\frac{5-AP}{5}=\frac{2AP}{13}$. Solving this gives $AP=\boxed{\frac{65}{23}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is right triangle ABC, C is at the lower left and marked with a right angle, B is at the upper left, and A is at the lower right. P is on side AC, Q is on side BC, segment PQ is parallel to AB, D is located on PQ and is the midpoint of PQ, segment AD connects from A to D, and AD is the angle bisector of angle BAC.

Reasoning: Because angle C = 90°, AB = 13, BC = 12, so AB is the hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem, AC = sqrt(AB^2 - BC^2) = sqrt(13^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(169 - 144) = 5. Let AP = x, then CP = AC - AP = 5 - x. Since PQ ∥ AB, and D is on PQ, so DP ∥ AB, therefore angle ADP = angle DAB. Also because AD bisects angle BAC, and P is on AC, so angle DAB = angle DAP. Thus angle ADP = angle DAP, triangle ADP is an isosceles triangle, giving PD = PA = x. D is the midpoint of PQ, so PQ = 2PD = 2x. From triangle ABC similar triangle PQC, corresponding sides AC and PC, AB and PQ are proportional, therefore CP/AC = PQ/AB. Substituting gives (5 - x)/5 = 2x/13. Solve the equation: 13(5 - x) = 10x, that is 65 - 13x = 10x, so 65 = 23x, x = 65/23. Therefore AP = 65/23.
